property_summary: After a Collect call, the contract's balance should decrease by at most the amount requested, and the sender's balance should increase by that amount only if the unlock condition (block.timestamp > unlockTime) is met.

After a Collect call that succeeds, the sender's unlockTime must equal the unlockTime set by the previous Put call; the buggy version changes unlockTime to the original _unlockTime, breaking this invariant.

After any Put then Collect, the collected amount must be at most the sender's recorded balance for that sender at the time of Collect, and that balance must equal the accumulated Put minus sent amounts.
After a Collect call that succeeds, the sender's unlockTime must be strictly greater than the block timestamp at the time of the preceding Put call.
After Collect, the sender's recorded unlockTime is always at least the block.timestamp at the time of the last Put.
Collect only succeeds when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, not when equal.
Collect cannot succeed when block.timestamp equals acc.unlockTime.
Collect only succeeds when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, not when equal.
Collect should revert when block.timestamp equals acc.unlockTime and the amount equals the balance exactly.
After any call to Collect(uint), the contract's own balance can only decrease when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, but not when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime.
The balance of an account after Collect with _am equal to its full balance should succeed, but the mutant requires strictly greater.
After Collect with _am equal to the caller's full balance, the caller's balance decreases only if the call succeeded (no revert).
If the caller's balance equals _am, Collect should succeed and reduce the balance by _am, regardless of whether _am is strictly less or equal.
Collect should succeed when the caller's balance equals exactly _am, transferring the funds and updating the balance.
After Collect with _am equal to the caller's full balance, the caller's balance becomes zero.
After Collect, the balance of the caller is unchanged (because the mutation removes the subtraction).
After Collect, the total call value sent to C from all callers is preserved across the function call
After calling Collect(uint256), the balance of the sender address stored in the Acc mapping is reduced by exactly the amount _am.
After Collect(uint256), the sum of Acc[any].balance and address(c).balance is invariant (conservation of value across all callers and the contract).
After Collect, the underflow check acc.balance >= _am, followed by the subtraction, implies that the sender's balance in Acc decreases by exactly _am.
